1.13 Development and verification

cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
uv run --python 3.13 python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'
uv run --python 3.13 python scripts/check-plugin-example.py

The Rust tests use synthetic sources. They cover path and range validation, read-only access and symlink rejection, exFAT timestamps and checksums, NFC names, composed reads across every piece boundary and change detection on their pieces, the DNG preview patch, JPEG EXIF injection, known preview stamps, map validation, the PMP timezone conventions, ratings capture from JPEG, DNG and sidecar XMP, sidecar naming and journaling, and harvesting by walk and by filesystem events. Integration tests run the server binary for config precedence, unknown settings and HTTP behavior. The Python tests drive the launcher against a mocked server and hdiutil: clean stops, busy detaches, identity mismatches and registration advice. The plugin check registers the hide example in a copy of the repository and serves it.

Beyond the tests, the workflows in this manual were exercised on real data. The PMP plugin resumed an interrupted card at its first new frame, and a new card was registered and ingested with the UTC convention. A previews library of 1.26 million stand-ins served its embedded previews byte for byte, and captured ratings written by Photo Mechanic and exiftool.

Never use real photos, catalogs or application databases as test fixtures.
